scope: Targeted offline contract for using original MCVar.dll through COM; no Windows/PCU execution.

claims.claim: IVar and IVar2 requested method declarations, IIDs, parameter order/types/flags, callback interface declarations and old/new normalized equality are decoded in MCVAR_COM_ABI.json.
Slots 9, 11 and 12 in old/new IVar/IVar2 vtables point to ReadVarAsync, ReadVarCyclic and RemoveCyclicVariables targets listed in the canonical map.
Both pCB and pDisp are declared client inputs; callback1/callback2 OnDataChanged parameter order and optionality are TypeLib facts.
Real async/cyclic public bodies call CRequestID::MakeCB, and MakeCB contains callback-result construction plus an indirect call through [ecx+0x1c].
claims.limitation: Interface/object identity and request-specific delivery are unresolved.

claims.claim: Which of pCB/pDisp is used for a particular request, exact callback route, DISPPARAMS/SAFEARRAY payload, thread/apartment, AddRef/Release order and delivery success.
pReqID pointer is stored at transaction +0x98; wrapper +0x04 separately stores transaction pointer; +0x20 is a distinct scalar use family.
Numeric ReqID production, registration, lookup, completion/cancel and cleanup linkage; whether removal drains callbacks.
ReadVarCyclic reaches internal reader paths that traverse cyclic records and directly call CCyclic construction with an owner-relative list argument; removal reaches internal removal paths.
SAFEARRAY element types/rank/bounds, rate units/defaults/revision semantics, deadband/critical filtering, cadence, independent quality delivery and complete scheduler/removal causality.

Conservative future client must retain callback objects and output storage through an application-defined quiescence condition, treat IDs as opaque, validate every VARIANT, use explicit operation ownership, and keep synchronous batched ReadVar fallback.
claims.limitation: These are defensive client policies, not vendor guarantees.
